name: Troefcall
description: Troefcall is a 4-player partnership trick-taking game from Suriname, also popular in the Netherlands. The 'trump caller' gets 5 cards first and declares trump. Teams try to win 7+ tricks. Winning first 7 in a row = 'Kap Partij' (5 pts). All 13 = 'Baunie' (15 pts). If Baunie attempted but failed, opponents score 2.

overview.description: Troefcall is a 4-player partnership trick-taking game from Suriname, also popular in the Netherlands. The 'trump caller' gets 5 cards first and declares trump. history.origins: Troefcall is a trick-taking game for four players played in the former Dutch colony Suriname and in the Surinamese community in the Netherlands. It has similarity to the Indian game Court Piece (Rang), possibly due to the presence of a significant minority of ethnic Indians in Suriname. The name (troefcall = 'trump call') mixes Dutch and English; the game was introduced to the Netherlands via Surinamese Dutch and is played across Surinamese population groups. Federations (TSBN in the Netherlands, STcB in Suriname) organize competitions.
timeline: 20th century: Played in Suriname; spread to the Netherlands via Surinamese Dutch community; federations (TSBN, STcB) organize competitions.

setup.dealing: Trump caller gets 5 first, declares trump. Then 5+4+4 to each.

rules.objective: Win the majority of tricks (at least 7 of 13) and be the first team to reach the agreed target score (e.g. 15, 20, or 50 points).
rules.gameplay: Trump caller leads. Follow suit. Trump if void. Win 7+ tricks for points. Kap Partij: Win first 7 consecutive = 5 pts. Baunie: Win all 13 = 15 pts. Failed Baunie = opponents get 2.

strategy.basic: Call trump in your longest suit. Win majority of tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Go for Kap if winning first 7; decide whether to push for Baunie.
strategy.advanced: Risk management: Baunie attempt vs safe Kap.

scoring.description: 7+ tricks = 2 pts. Kap = 5 pts. Baunie = 15 pts. Failed Baunie = -2 to opponents.
